cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles by the River Kebar (Ezekiel 1:1-3). Far away, the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem (Ezekiel 24:2). Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel.
God calls him son of man, and the news is heavy. He's about to take away the desire of Ezekiel's eyes with a fatal blow.

cards.question: When God takes away the desire of Ezekiel's eyes, Ezekiel is allowed to weep and let his tears flow.

cards.text: God says to groan quietly and not mourn for the dead. Friend, when they slid me into that junk drawer, I did NOT groan quietly.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel not to dress like a mourner. What does God tell him to wear instead?
God tells Ezekiel not to cover his lips. What else does God tell him not to do?
Ezekiel speaks to the people in the morning. What happens that evening?

cards.text: The next morning, Ezekiel does just as he was commanded. I bet the people can't stop staring, and finally they ask him something.

cards.question: The people watch Ezekiel act this way after his wife's death. What do they ask him?

answers.text: What his actions mean for them
Why God took his wife away
Why he isn't angry at God

cards.text: Ezekiel answers with the word of the LORD for the house of Israel. He lost the desire of his eyes, and now God says Israel is about to lose the desire of theirs.

cards.question: God says He is about to desecrate the desire of Israel's eyes, the pride of their power. What is it?
God also says the sons and daughters the people left behind will fall by the sword.

cards.text: Then Ezekiel tells them they'll do just as he has done. No covering their lips, and no bread of mourners.

cards.question: Ezekiel says that on that day, the people will take off their turbans and sandals.
Ezekiel says the people won't mourn or weep on that day. What will happen to them instead?

answers.text: They will waste away because of their sins
They will be comforted by their neighbors
They will quickly forget all their sorrow

cards.text: Then come God's words again: 'Thus Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do everything that he has done.'

cards.question: When all this happens, what does God say the people will know?

answers.text: That He is the Lord GOD
That Ezekiel is a true priest

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel about the day He takes away their stronghold, their pride and joy, and their sons and daughters. Who will come and tell Ezekiel the news?
On that same day, something changes for Ezekiel himself. What is it?

answers.text: He will speak and no longer be mute
He will be set free from his exile
He will see Jerusalem with his eyes

cards.text: I went quiet for years in that junk drawer, and now I can't STOP talking. So Ezekiel will be a sign to them, and they will know that He is the LORD.

findings.problem: The stop has 12 choice cards: 9 multiple choice, 3 true or false and no fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to the backstory: he groaned loudly when he was slid into the drawer. The backstory says that in the drawer 'He didn't talk much. He didn't joke at all.' The joke also contradicts card 20, where he says he 'went quiet' in the drawer. It also lands on the card right after God announces the fatal blow to the desire of Ezekiel's eyes, so it reads as making light of a grief moment instead of fitting it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Speak a word to anyone' is arguable from the passage. Verse 27 says Ezekiel will 'speak and no longer be mute,' so a baker could argue he is currently not to speak.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'Finally they ask him' adds a delay the text doesn't give. Verse 19 simply says 'Then the people asked me.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'Act this way' points back to card 8, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say what Ezekiel is doing (not mourning, turban and sandals on).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Their city walls' is close to the passage. Verse 25 lists 'their stronghold' alongside 'the desire of their eyes,' so a baker could argue the walls are right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The baker has never been told that Ezekiel is mute. Earlier cards show him speaking to the people (verses 18 and 20), so 'no longer be mute' can't be reasoned out and seems to contradict what was told. 'On that same day' also points back to card 18, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: 'I went quiet for years in that junk drawer' stretches the backstory, which says he gave up 'for a while' before welcoming newcomers. It also contradicts the card 4 joke, where he says he did NOT groan quietly in the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 10 and 13 are flat retellings with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice, such as a reaction, a storyteller's line or a disbelief beat suited to the moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
